title: Multi-head attention
goal:
Implement multi-head self-attention from Section 3.2.2, where $\operatorname{head}_i = \operatorname{Attention}(XW_i^Q, XW_i^K, XW_i^V)$ and the output is $\operatorname{Concat}(\operatorname{head}_1, \dots, \operatorname{head}_h)\,W^O$.

Write `multi_head_attention(X, Wq, Wk, Wv, Wo, h, mask=None)`. `X` has shape `(n, d_model)`. Each of `Wq`, `Wk`, `Wv`, and `Wo` has shape `(d_model, d_model)`, and `d_model` is divisible by `h`. Column block `i` of `Wq` is $W_i^Q$, which has shape `(d_model, d_k)` with `d_k = d_model // h`. The function returns an array of shape `(n, d_model)`. The optional boolean `mask` has shape `(n, n)`.

The starter provides finished `softmax` and `scaled_dot_product_attention` helpers that accept a leading head axis. You write the projection, the split into heads, and the merge.
hints: Project first: `Q = X @ Wq` has shape `(n, d_model)`. The same goes for `K` and `V`.
Split with `Q.reshape(n, h, d_k)`, then `.transpose(1, 0, 2)` to get `(h, n, d_k)`. Skipping the transpose mixes tokens into heads.
The helper broadcasts a `(n, n)` mask over the head axis, so pass `mask` through unchanged.
To merge, transpose the output back to `(n, h, d_v)`, reshape to `(n, h * d_v)`, and multiply by `Wo`.
